paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: wisdom isn't just for knowing things, it's for living well. The writer says to preserve sound judgment and discernment, and that they will be "life to your soul" (Proverbs 3:22). Hold on to them and you can walk safely and sleep sweetly, because "the LORD will be your confidence" (Proverbs 3:26). I spent years awake in a junk drawer, so believe me, that kind of rest is worth more than any cookie.

Then the writer shows where wisdom goes to work: right next door. Don't withhold good from the deserving when it's within your power to act (Proverbs 3:27). Don't plot against a neighbor who "trustfully dwells beside you" (Proverbs 3:29). Don't envy the violent man either (Proverbs 3:31). So wisdom isn't only what you know, it's how you treat the person on the other side of the fence, and help that's in your hands today shouldn't wait for tomorrow.

The passage ends with pairs, and every pair shows whose side the LORD is on. He is "a friend to the upright" (Proverbs 3:32), and He "gives grace to the humble" (Proverbs 3:34). Friend, I'm not saying a humble baker never burns a batch, because I've burned PLENTY. But the humble are the ones who walk with the LORD, and "the wise will inherit honor" (Proverbs 3:35). So hold on to wisdom, do good while it's in your hands, and stay humble.
